questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Uganda?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uganda article.

questions.proof: The capital and largest city is Kampala.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Uganda?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Uganda on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uganda article.

questions.proof: It shares land borders with five countries including the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west, Kenya to the east, South Sudan to the north, Rwanda to the south-west, and Tanzania to the south.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Uganda?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uganda article.

questions.proof: The official languages of Uganda are English and Swahili.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Uganda?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uganda article.

questions.proof: The currency is the Ugandan Shilling.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Besides Lake _____ and Lake Kyoga, there are Lake Albert, Lake Edward and the smaller Lake George.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Lake”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Uganda article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: Besides Lake Victoria and Lake Kyoga, there are Lake Albert, Lake Edward and the smaller Lake George.
